column3: The Hebrew repeats the unfaithfulness root in a verb and noun and uses the same term for what is devoted both times; BSB says “acted unfaithfully” and varies “devoted to destruction” with “set apart.”
The Hebrew has both “said” and “saying”; BSB gives a single “told.”
The Hebrew directly prohibits the whole people going up and names the town’s inhabitants only as “they”; BSB says there is “no need” and explicitly names “the people of Ai.”
The Hebrew says the men came “from the people”; BSB does not include that phrase.
The Hebrew has singular “the heart of the people,” which became water; BSB uses plural “hearts” and says they became “like water.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Joshua fell to the ground and has singular collective “their head”; BSB says “fell facedown” and uses plural “heads.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the Amorite” and actively says “to destroy us”; BSB has plural “the Amorites” and the passive “to be destroyed.”
The Hebrew says Israel turned its “neck”; BSB says “its back and run,” supplying a separate running action.
The Hebrew uses a singular collective name for the Canaanite and says to “cut off” the name; BSB uses plural “Canaanites” and “wipe out.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “and also” five times; BSB varies the links and uses “Indeed” once.
The Hebrew says they turn their neck before their enemies, without an explicit running verb; BSB has “turn their backs and run.”
The Hebrew repeats “from among you” in the removal clause; BSB says simply “remove them.”
The Hebrew repeats the verb for catching as the LORD selects each group; BSB uses “selects.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “with fire”; BSB says “burned.”
The Hebrew uses the passive of catching for the tribe’s selection; BSB says “was selected.”

The Hebrew first uses singular “the clan of Judah,” then actively says “he caught” the Zerahite clan, and explicitly says “man by man.” BSB has plural “clans,” a passive selection, and omits “man by man” here.
The Hebrew says “his house”; BSB explicitly names “the family of Zabdi.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has both “answered” and “said” and repeats “thus and thus”; BSB has “replied” and a single “This is what I did.”
The Hebrew calls the gold a “tongue”; BSB says “a bar.”
The Hebrew refers to the hidden object with a feminine singular form; BSB says “it all.”
The Hebrew refers to the objects with “them”; BSB makes them explicit as “the things.”
The Hebrew names a “tongue of gold” and uses singular “his ox” and “his donkey”; BSB has “bar of gold” and plural “oxen and donkeys.”
The Hebrew says they stoned him, burned “them,” and then stoned “them”; BSB rearranges the plural stoning before the burning and explicitly names “the others” and “their bodies.”
The Hebrew says “over him” and actively says “he called” the place’s name; BSB names Achan and uses the passive “is called.”
